thread:
maria: Observed a jump in funcall parse errors on the new PTQ canary. baseline ~0.15% -> 2.9% on a 5k sample. example traces uploaded.
josh: Any raw examples here?
maria: pasted two from the dump:
```
1) {
  "action": "lookup",
  "args": {"term": "coffee",},
  }
2) {"action":"buy","args":{"id":"xyz"}
	
```
vikram: trailing comma + extra closing brace in 1, newline truncation in 2. Could be suffix noise from quantized decoder or streaming chunk boundary. What's canary config?
maria: model=raven-lite:v2-int8-ptq, streaming=true, kvprefix=on, batch=12, prompt includes example JSON tool call.
ella: quick mitigation: enable a conservative postprocess that strips trailing commas and tries to balance braces before calling the JSON parser. We already have a tiny `struct_heal` shim in the agent runtime. Gate it with a canary flag so we can count repairs.
josh: please also run the identical prompt set on the fp16 mirror to confirm regression. If fp16 is clean then PTQ is suspect.
maria: fp16 mirror results: parse failures 0.18%. So clearly higher on int8.
vikram: plan proposal: run 4 experiments in parallel:
- A: int8 baseline (streaming=true, kvprefix=on, batch=12)
- B: int8 streaming=false, kvprefix=off, batch=4
- C: int8 + prompt-sentinel (append \"\n<<<END>>>\")
- D: fp16 baseline (control)
We should sample 1k per arm and check original_parse_fail, repaired_by_heal, retried_on_fp, final_nonparse.
maria: started jobs: canary id=ptq-1799998765-A..D. deploy-bot: Canary jobs kicked off.
deploy-bot: Canary suite started: job_group=ptq-1799998765, tasks=4, s3_prefix=s3://canary-logs/raven-lite/1799998765/
josh: I'll reduce batch to 4 for B and C to reduce inter-request interleaving. Also will keep latency snapshots.
ella: add a metric to the canary dashboards: parse_repair_rate and parse_regression_delta (int8 vs fp16). Also log the raw model suffix tokens around the parse boundary (10 tokens before/after) so research can inspect decoder jitter.
vikram: if B (no streaming, no kvprefix) still fails much higher than fp16 then it's possibly PTQ internal quant-decoder noise; escalate to research to audit kernels. If B looks like fp16 then streaming/kvprefix interaction likely the cause.
maria: ops: pause any wider rollout until we have canary results. I've toggled the rollout hold.
josh: short-term runbook for prod: enable `struct_heal` middleware behind flag + single retry on a float variant (retry_on_fp=true, retries=1, backoff=150ms). This will mask transient parser flakiness for customers while we debug.
ella: careful: we must record how many repairs hide real regressions. Add telemetry fields: original_parse_status, repaired_by_struct_heal, retry_reached_fp, final_status, raw_suffix_tokens.
maria: uploaded the first 500 traces to S3. URL in case notes.
vikram: running the microbench to reproduce with deterministic seed (tokenizer seed + attention seed) and will capture attention scores. Command I used:
```bash
rw-canary run --model raven-lite:v2-int8-ptq --sample 1000 --seed 42 --streaming=false --kvprefix=off --tag microbench-ptq
```
josh: good. Also run the RDF-style prompt that previously triggered trailing-comma artifacts.
maria: next steps: await canary metrics (~30-45m). If repairs cover >60% of failures and fp16 unaffected, we can opt to keep struct_heal + retry patch for 24-48h, but must plan a follow-on engineering task: "quant decoder jitter audit" with research and runtime teams.
ella: I'll prepare the struct_heal PR with feature flag and telemetry. Will include unit tests showing closures of unbalanced braces and removal of trailing commas.
maria: thanks all. tagging @vikram to coordinate research escalation if B fails. :thumbsup:
